partially_working.item: Architecture-documented data flow: Historical Journal -> Validation/Outcome Engine
partially_working.evidence: docs/architecture.md, section 3.13, states the target data flow as 'Historical Journal → Validation/Outcome Engine → Probability Engine'. Grepped server.ts for any reference to outcomeRecords or /api/outcome inside the Journal functions (appendJournalEntry, JournalEntry type, deriveRollingVerdict, buildJournalText, buildJournalHtml) - found NONE. What was actually built instead: the client calls POST /api/outcome/record directly from triggerHaikuVerdicts() at the moment a NEW verdict is computed in the browser, entirely independent of whether/how that verdict is ever written to the Historical Journal. The two systems currently run in parallel, not in the documented sequence.

The architecture document's Journal-sourced version was not re-checked against the implementation before this verification pass.

incorrect_or_risky.item: Bounded record array can silently drop an unevaluated PENDING record
incorrect_or_risky.evidence: server.ts: if (outcomeRecords.length > OUTCOME_MAX_RECORDS) outcomeRecords.shift(); - this evicts the OLDEST record regardless of its status. If the array reaches 500 entries, a still-PENDING record (one whose outcome window hasn't completed yet) can be silently discarded before ever reaching a terminal status - it simply vanishes rather than being marked INCOMPLETE_* or logged. At current recording cadence (once per verdict-change episode per symbol, not per poll), this would take a long time to trigger in practice, but it is a real, unaddressed edge case, not a hypothetical one.
incorrect_or_risky.severity: Low likelihood given current volume, but a genuine correctness gap against the 'incomplete windows are excluded rather than guessed' principle - a silently vanished PENDING record is arguably worse than an explicit INCOMPLETE status, since it leaves no trace at all.

recommended_next_action.smallest_necessary_fix: Wire the Outcome Engine's recording trigger to fire from the Historical Journal write path (appendJournalEntry / the journal-verdict derivation) instead of - or in addition to - the current client-side verdict-change trigger, so the actual documented data flow (Historical Journal -> Validation/Outcome Engine) is real rather than just described. This is the one change needed to close the architecture-compliance gap; everything else (evaluation logic, statuses, statistics, tests) is already sound and would not need to change.
recommended_next_action.secondary_fix: Change the 500-record cap eviction to skip/protect still-PENDING records (e.g. evict the oldest DETERMINATE/INCOMPLETE record first, or raise the cap), so a record can never silently disappear before reaching a terminal status.
recommended_next_action.not_recommended_yet: Building the Probability Engine - correctly deferred, since even after the above fix, real historical sample size will still be small; Probability Engine work should wait until the Journal-linked recording has been live long enough to accumulate a meaningful determinate-record count (see MIN_SAMPLE_SIZE = 5 in outcome-engine.ts, and note actual production data will need far more than that for a genuinely useful probability figure).
